summary: Frontend-only verification of Verdaleaf live-camera feature at https://codebase-reader-21.preview.emergentagent.com/dashboard. Injected a canvas.captureStream()-based fake MediaStream via add_init_script (since the automation browser can't be launched with --use-fake-device-for-media-stream flags) to simulate a real MediaStream with painted frames. Verified: control separation, real video frames rendering, shutter->review flow, Use-photo->preview->/api/detect (ONE successful 200 with real diagnosis text on the camera-captured base64 JPEG), MediaStream track cleanup after both close and Use-photo, permission-denied path, unsupported-browser fallback to native capture input, dark-mode class applied, and desktop rendering. Found ONE clear regression: Retake leaves the live <video> blank because the getUserMedia useEffect does not re-attach streamRef.current to the newly-remounted <video> element.

critical_code_review_comments: CameraCapture.jsx: The <video> element is unmounted whenever a shot is being reviewed. Because attaching srcObject happens inside the getUserMedia useEffect (dependency [facing, stop]), Retake results in a black video. This is a functional regression, not cosmetic.

CameraCapture.jsx: useEffect return only sets `cancelled = true`; it does not stop() the stream on unmount. Cleanup relies on the second `useEffect(() => stop, [stop])`. That works, but it's easy to accidentally break by changing the dep order. Consider stopping inside the same effect's return.

CameraCapture.jsx line 43: `width/height: { ideal: 1920 }` requests a square-ish max — fine, but `enumerateDevices` runs unconditionally after getUserMedia and requires camera perms; on rejection it's already gated by try/catch — OK.
UploadZone.jsx supportsLiveCamera guard is evaluated once at render time — fine for this app.
No accessibility label on camera-shutter-btn beyond aria-label='Take photo' — good. Retake and Use photo have text labels — good.
seed_data_creation: None. One live /api/detect call was made with a canvas-generated JPEG and it returned 200 with a plausible 'Not a plant image' diagnosis, proving the captured base64 payload is accepted by the backend.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Automation browser (mcp_browser_automation) cannot be launched with --use-fake-device-for-media-stream. To exercise a real MediaStream in this env, inject via page.add_init_script a stub of navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia that returns canvas.captureStream(30). IMPORTANT: return a NEW stream each call — the component's useEffect calls stop() on the previous stream before requesting a new one, so a shared stream will be 'ended' by the time the video attaches. See iteration_4 script for a working pattern. Live-detect was already burned once (200 OK) so the happy-path is proven; no need to hit /api/detect again unless you're verifying a fix. Retake bug should be the primary retest target.
rca_of_the_issue: CameraCapture renders `{shot ? <img/> : <video/>}`. React unmounts <video> when entering review and mounts a NEW <video> element on Retake. The stream is attached to `videoRef.current.srcObject` only inside the getUserMedia useEffect, whose dependencies are [facing, stop]. Neither changes on Retake, so the effect does not re-run and the new <video> DOM node never receives srcObject. Reproduction: open camera -> shutter -> retake -> observe camera-video has videoWidth=0, srcObject=null, paused=true; second shutter press then triggers `Camera is still warming up` toast. Mitigation options in action_items.
